newsitem.title: FRANCE: PRESS DIGEST - France - Le Monde April 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - France - Le Monde April 22.

text.p: These are leading stories in afternoon daily Le Monde.
-- Prime Minister Alain Juppe rules out a shift in economic policy, will launch his campaign for the May 25 and June 1 parliamentary election today.

He is expected to present his platform today to the parliamentary majority, stressing state reform, economic initiative and cuts in labour charges, France's role in the construction of Europe and its single currency.
-- Juppe plans to freeze spending at current levels in 1998.
-- State-owned bank Caisse des Depots et Consignations posts 1996 profit close to four billion francs.

-- Pechiney targets 11 percent return on investment after a two-year cost cutting plan is implemented. Its ANC subsidiary opens fish-canning plant in Brazil's Minas Gerais state, a 400-million-franc investment.
-- Unions representing a majority of cockpit crews at British Airways subsidiary TAT-Air Liberte reach agreement, strike to be called off this afternoon. Other unions to continue negotiations.
-- Finance Minister Jean Arthuis rules out a recapitalisation of state bank Credit Lyonnais.
